paragraphs.title: David Turns to Jonathan for Help

easy.explanation: David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came to Jonathan.
David said that Saul was seeking his life.
easy.q: Whom did David fear was seeking his life?

easy.explanation: Jonathan promised to do whatever David's soul desired.
easy.q: What did Jonathan promise to do for David?

answers: He wanted to return to Ramah
medium.explanation: David described the immediate danger he faced from Saul.
medium.q: Why did David say there was only a step between him and death?

answers: Saul would reveal anything great or small to him
medium.explanation: Jonathan said that his father would show him anything great or small.
medium.q: Why did Jonathan think Saul would not hide his intention from him?

medium.explanation: “God forbid” strongly rejects the thought that David should die.
medium.q: What does “God forbid” express in Jonathan's reply?

answers: He felt the danger was immediate
He wanted to return to Saul
challenge.explanation: David's words show that he believed Saul's threat was urgent and deadly.
challenge.q: What does David's continued pleading with Jonathan show?

answers: He asks David whether he wants to eat
He invites David to propose a plan and promises to help
He says that he is hiding
challenge.explanation: Jonathan invites David to tell him what he wants done.
challenge.q: What does Jonathan mean by asking, “Whatsoever thy soul desireth”?

answers: David says he cannot identify any offense deserving death
David asks Saul directly for forgiveness
challenge.explanation: David insists that he has committed no sin justifying Saul's pursuit.
challenge.q: How do “What have I done?” and “what is mine iniquity?” fit together?

paragraphs.title: The Test and the Covenant Between David and Jonathan

easy.explanation: David said that the next day was the New Moon and that he would not sit with the king at meat.
easy.q: At which meal did David plan to be absent?

easy.explanation: David asked Jonathan to say that he had gone to Bethlehem.
easy.q: Where did David say he wanted to go?

easy.explanation: David said, “if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself.”
easy.q: What did David ask Jonathan to do if he had iniquity?

answers: To see how Saul reacted to David's absence from the meal
To test whether the lad could shoot
To see whether David could reach Bethlehem
medium.explanation: They planned to observe Saul's response when David was absent from the New Moon meal.
medium.q: What test did David and Jonathan plan?

answers: Saul saying that it was well and that David would have peace
medium.explanation: A peaceful response would show that no evil had been determined against David.
medium.q: What would show that Saul did not intend to harm David?

medium.explanation: David asks Jonathan to treat him with covenant kindness and faithfulness.
medium.q: What does “deal kindly with thy servant” mean in this passage?

answers: The covenant concerned only the meal
He wanted kindness to continue to their households
challenge.explanation: David asked that Jonathan's kindness not be cut off from his house forever.
challenge.q: Why did David connect the covenant with Jonathan's house?

answers: Tell David the truth and send him away in peace
challenge.explanation: Jonathan promised to show David the truth and send him away in peace.
challenge.q: What did Jonathan promise to do if he learned that evil was determined against David?

answers: Their bond was deep and faithful
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the depth of Jonathan's love for David.
challenge.q: What does “he loved him as he loved his own soul” reveal?

paragraphs.title: The Arrow Signal and the Secret Message

answers: On the third day of the week
easy.explanation: Jonathan said, “To morrow is the new moon: and thou shalt be missed.”
easy.q: When did Jonathan say David would be missed from his seat?

easy.explanation: Jonathan said, “I will shoot three arrows.”
easy.q: How many arrows did Jonathan plan to shoot?

answers: David should come to the meal
David had been sent away and should flee
easy.explanation: Arrows beyond the lad would mean that the Lord had sent David away.
easy.q: What would arrows shot beyond the lad mean?

answers: There was peace and no hurt
medium.explanation: Jonathan would say that there was peace and no hurt if the arrows were near.
medium.q: What would arrows on the near side of the lad mean?

answers: To teach the lad to shoot
To bring the arrows to Saul
medium.explanation: The shooting instructions allowed Jonathan to send David a hidden message.
medium.q: Why did Jonathan use a lad and arrows?

answers: You will be found in another place
You will be absent from your seat
medium.explanation: David would be absent from his usual place at the king's meal.
medium.q: In this context, what does “thou shalt be missed” mean?

answers: The message to David would remain secret
The lad would shoot more arrows
challenge.explanation: Only Jonathan and David were to understand the meaning of the signal.
challenge.q: Why was it important that the lad did not understand the arrows?

answers: Near arrows meant danger, and distant arrows meant peace
Near arrows meant peace, and distant arrows meant David should flee
challenge.explanation: The location of the arrows indicated whether David was safe or needed to leave.
challenge.q: What was the practical difference between the two arrow signals?

answers: The Lord would witness and uphold their covenant
The Lord was angry and separating them
challenge.explanation: They placed their covenant and its obligations under the Lord's witness.
challenge.q: What does “the Lord be between thee and me for ever” mean?

paragraphs.title: The New Moon Meal and Saul's Anger

easy.explanation: The passage says that David's place was empty.
easy.q: Whose place was empty at the king's table?

answers: Something had happened and he was unclean
He had been injured in the field
easy.explanation: Saul thought David might be ceremonially unclean.
easy.q: What did Saul first think about David's absence?

easy.explanation: Jonathan explained David's absence to Saul.
easy.q: Who told Saul that David had gone to Bethlehem?

answers: David was expected to sit in his place at the meal
medium.explanation: Saul expected the son of Jesse to attend the meal.
medium.q: Why did Saul notice David's absence again on the second day?

answers: He agreed to send David away
He became angry and ordered David to be brought to him
medium.explanation: Saul's anger was kindled, and he declared that David should surely die.
medium.q: How did Saul respond to Jonathan's explanation?

medium.explanation: Saul used the phrase as an insulting rebuke against Jonathan.
medium.q: What kind of expression was “thou son of the perverse rebellious woman”?

answers: He loved David and knew no offense had been shown
He had not heard Saul's words
challenge.explanation: Jonathan asked what David had done and defended him as innocent.
challenge.q: Why did Jonathan oppose David's death?

answers: Saul had determined to kill David
challenge.explanation: The attack showed Jonathan that Saul was determined to slay David.
challenge.q: What did Jonathan understand when Saul cast the javelin?

answers: He was grieved for David and ashamed by Saul's treatment
challenge.explanation: Jonathan was grieved for David because his father had done him shame.
challenge.q: Why did Jonathan refuse to eat on the second day?

paragraphs.title: The Message Is Delivered and the Farewell

easy.explanation: Jonathan went into the field with David and a little lad.
easy.q: Who went with Jonathan to the field?

easy.explanation: Jonathan shot an arrow beyond the lad.
easy.q: Where did Jonathan shoot the arrow?

easy.explanation: They kissed one another and wept together.
easy.q: How did David and Jonathan part?

answers: He could return to the meal
Saul knew nothing of his absence
medium.explanation: The arrows beyond the lad signaled that David had been sent away.
medium.q: What message did David understand from the arrows?

answers: So the lad would not know the secret message
So the lad could bring Saul
So the lad could guard David
medium.explanation: The lad knew nothing about the matter, allowing David and Jonathan to speak privately.
medium.q: Why did Jonathan send the lad into the city before speaking with David?

answers: A decision to live in Jerusalem
Their oath that the Lord would be between them and their seed
A promise to attend the meal
medium.explanation: They reaffirmed their oath concerning themselves and their descendants.
medium.q: What did David and Jonathan renew in their farewell?

answers: The separation was painful and their bond was deep
They were angry with each other
challenge.explanation: Their tears and embrace reveal the pain of separation and the depth of their friendship.
challenge.q: What does their prolonged weeping show?

answers: The arrows allow Jonathan to protect David faithfully
The arrows were only a game
challenge.explanation: By using the signal, Jonathan truthfully warned David and kept his covenant.
challenge.q: How does the arrow message relate to Jonathan's covenant promise?

answers: The oath extended to their descendants and future generations
The covenant lasted only through the meal
Jonathan wanted to leave David forever
challenge.explanation: Mentioning their seed shows that the covenant was intended to continue beyond their own lives.
challenge.q: What does “between my seed and thy seed for ever” emphasize?
